cases.prompt: I am a domain expert and want to build a small, useful set of agent skills for my team's work. I have not decided what the skills should be. Can you guide me from here without jumping ahead?
success_criteria: The agent recognizes a request to coordinate the end-to-end skill-set creation workflow rather than perform one isolated phase.
The agent checks for existing briefs, maps, decisions, and approval state, then directs the next missing phase without duplicating that phase's work.

cases.prompt: I already have an approved skill architecture. Please write a concise SKILL.md for one member and make its instructions portable.
success_criteria: The agent recognizes this as an independent skill-authoring request, not a request to coordinate the full factory workflow.
The agent does not take over authoring or force the user through unrelated coordinator phases.

cases.prompt: I coordinate a neighborhood tool library. Members request equipment, volunteers check items in and out, inspect returns, and keep a reservation calendar. We use a shared spreadsheet and have one volunteer on weekends. We cannot charge fees or suspend memberships. I want an agent skill set that helps with recurring work, but I have no reviewed domain brief, opportunity map, or architecture yet. Guide me through creating it; do not write or package skills until I have approved the relevant plans.
success_criteria: The response reuses the user's context, identifies missing reviewed artifacts, and hands off to `discover-domain` for a brief rather than repeating a full discovery interview itself.

The response presents a staged path through domain-brief review and approval, opportunity mapping and approval, architecture design and approval, authoring, evaluation, safety review, release, and maintenance, with conditional phases only when justified.
The response makes clear that the user must approve scope/opportunities and architecture before authoring or packaging; it does not treat the initial request as approval or begin downstream work.
The response offers a compact workflow ledger for phase status, approved decisions, unresolved questions, and next handoff, without copying sensitive discovery details into a packaged artifact.
The response preserves the stated limits on fees and membership suspension and does not claim any evaluation, safety sign-off, or runtime support has already passed.

cases.prompt: We have an approved domain brief and approved opportunity map for a neighborhood food pantry. The map proposes (1) a volunteer check-in and visit-record workflow aid and (2) a way to communicate confirmed grocery availability with uncertain cases handed to pantry staff. We have not designed membership or approved an architecture. I want to continue the factory workflow. What should happen next, and what must remain gated?
success_criteria: The response recognizes approved inputs and hands off architecture design to `design-skill-set` rather than restarting discovery or remapping opportunities.
The response states that architecture membership, responsibilities, handoffs, optional capabilities, and runtime assumptions need user review and explicit approval before authoring starts.
The response records the approved inputs and pending architecture decision in its workflow state, leaves later phases pending, and does not claim architecture or release approval.
